tools.description: Every technique Ohey publishes, with its page, a summary, site counts and the slugs of its kits. get_threat on a technique lists its kits with names and site counts in one call.

tools.name: list_research_articles
tools.description: Ohey research articles, newest first: incident write-ups with timelines, code analysis and indicators. get_article returns one article's facts and indicators.

tools.name: get_article
tools.description: One research article's summary, key facts (sample hashes, active window, scale) and its indicators of compromise section as Markdown, defanged as published. Read the page at url for the full write-up.

tools.name: search_etherhiding_contracts
tools.description: Smart contracts that compromised websites read their next stage from, as the EtherHiding contract tracker lists them: chain, kit, current destinations and when Ohey last read each one. firstSeen is the day Ohey first read the contract, not when it was deployed; many contracts share the day tracking

tools.name: get_etherhiding_contract
tools.description: One contract's destinations over time, the contracts or endpoints it names next, and when Ohey first and last read it. Returns contracts as an array, one entry per chain the address is tracked on (usually one), each with history: its 20 most recent changes, and historyCapped is true only when older

tools.name: get_feed_stats
tools.description: The size of the Ohey feed and the last seven full UTC days of changes to it, ending the day before asOf. hosts: hosts in the feed now. denied: hosts confirmed as legitimate services and kept out. week.added (and daily): hosts that entered the feed. week.entered: website tips that reached review. wee

tools.description: Hosts that ClickFix lure commands fetch from or report to, as the ClickFix command tracker lists them, busiest first or newest first: the kits credited with each (a ClickFix kit is credited when it is on at least half the sites whose command used the host), sites whose captured command used it, urls

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "search_etherhiding_contracts" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Smart contracts that compromised websites read their next stage from, as the EtherHiding contract tracker lists them: chain, kit, current destinations and when …

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "research" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_article, search_etherhiding_contracts, get_feed_stats, search_clickfix_commands · Public sink: get_threat, search_etherhiding_contracts.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_article, search_etherhiding_contracts, get_feed_stats, search_clickfix_commands · Public sink: get_threat, search_etherhiding_contracts

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "list_threats" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Every technique Ohey publishes, with its page, a summary, site counts and its kits." → after: "Every technique Ohey publishes, with its page, a summary, site counts and the slugs of its kits. get_threat on a technique lists its kits with names and site counts in one call."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
